dialogue:
RPh: Good afternoon, this is Marcus at Brookside Family Pharmacy. Am I speaking with Ms. Parkinson?
Pt: You are. Rosemary - but everyone calls me Rosie.
RPh: Rosie, I'm calling about the medicines you brought home from Stillwater Regional. Can you confirm your date of birth?
Pt: March 14th, 1958.
RPh: Thanks. Dr. Hill sent the discharge list on October 9. Do you have your bottles?
Pt: Right here. Dr. Hill is a sweetheart, but I nearly fainted walking up the hill to her office on Far Hills Avenue.
RPh: That fits. Your lisinopril went from 20 mg down to 10 mg because your pressure dropped when you stood - 96/58 standing.
Pt: So the old 20s go in the drawer?
RPh: Bring them in and we'll dispose of them. The carbidopa-levodopa stays 25/100, one and a half tablets at 7, 11 and 3.
Pt: That one helps. The shake in my right hand is maybe a 3 out of 10 now.
RPh: Good. I also see a fill last week for metoclopramide. Who prescribed that?
Pt: A PA at the walk-in on Wilmington Pike, Tomasz Wren. Stomach bug. My son Declan picked it up at the CVS.
RPh: Metoclopramide can make Parkinson's disease worse, so please hold it. I'll ask the prescriber about ondansetron if you still need something.
Pt: Fine, I only took two. The Miralax I mix in my coffee before I go in - I still do the library aide job at Orchard Hollow Elementary.
RPh: Perfect. Call me at 937-555-0148 with any questions; Dr. Hill's office faxes us at 937-555-0177.
Pt: Thanks, Marcus. You're a gem.
note:
BROOKSIDE FAMILY PHARMACY -- TRANSITIONS-OF-CARE MEDICATION RECONCILIATION
2290 Kettering Blvd, Kettering, OH 45439 | Ph 937-555-0148 | Fax 937-555-0177

Patient: PARKINSON, ROSEMARY ("Rosie")  DOB 03/14/1958 (68 y)  Rx profile BFP-0042719
Stillwater Regional Medical Center MRN 00-7718-264  Admit 10/05/2026  Discharge 10/09/2026
Discharging prescriber: Annette Hill, MD, NPI 1730582946, office fax 937-555-0193
Pharmacist: Marcus Oyelaran, PharmD (M.O.)  Phone review 10/13/2026

S: 68-year-old woman with Parkinson's disease (dx 2019, Hoehn and Yahr stage 2) and essential hypertension, discharged after orthostatic presyncope. Ms. Parkinson rates right-hand tremor 3/10. Lives alone; son Declan runs errands. Part-time library aide at Orchard Hollow Elementary.

O: BP 124/76 sitting, 96/58 standing. eGFR 71. Outside fills checked via PDMP and CVS #4471 (Wilmington Pike).

MEDICATIONS (home -> discharge -> action)
1. Carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 1.5 tab TID at 0700/1100/1500 -> unchanged -> continue.
2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily -> 10 mg daily -> return old bottle for disposal.
3. Polyethylene glycol 3350 17 g daily -> new -> continue for constipation.
4. Docusate 100 mg BID -> stopped.
5. Metoclopramide 10 mg q6h PRN (filled 10/02/2026; Tomasz Wren, PA-C, DEA MW5583021) -> not on discharge list -> HOLD.

A: (1) Drug-disease interaction: metoclopramide is a dopamine antagonist and can worsen parkinsonism. (2) Retired lisinopril strength in the home. (3) Constipation controlled.

P: Faxed Dr. Hill and PA Wren 10/13/26 suggesting ondansetron 4 mg ODT PRN. Follow-up call 10/20/2026. Refills: https://brooksidefamilyrx.com/refill or rx@brooksidefamilyrx.com.
-- M. Oyelaran, PharmD

BACKGROUND
71-year-old retired marine engineer (35 yrs with Konkan Coastal Shipping) with type 2 DM x 18 yrs, diabetic kidney disease CKD G3b A2 and dyslipidaemia. Daughter Shirin, a teacher at Tardeo Model High School, brought all strips and bottles in a carry bag. Family calls him "Cyru"; admits extra sweets since Navroze. Two episodes of sweating and tremor at ~4 am last week, relieved by sugar.

LABS (accession NVH/BIO/26/118429, collected 09-10-2026)
HbA1c 9.4 % | FBS 212 mg/dL | S. creatinine 1.78 mg/dL | eGFR 38 mL/min/1.73 m2 (CKD-EPI 2021) | K+ 5.6 mmol/L | UACR 146 mg/g | LDL-C 92 mg/dL

MEDICINES FOUND (source)
1. Tab Metformin 1000 mg 1-0-1 (a)
2. Tab Glimepiride 2 mg 1-0-0 (a)
3. Tab Gliclazide MR 60 mg 1-0-0 (b)
4. Tab Telmisartan 40 mg 0-0-1 (b)
5. Tab Spironolactone 25 mg 1-0-0 (old Rx of 2024, still being refilled)
6. Tab Atorvastatin 20 mg 0-0-1 (a)
7. Tab Dapagliflozin 10 mg 1-0-0 (b)
8. Herbal "sugar churna", brand unknown (self)
Daughter asked whether he should also take a baby aspirin - not advised for primary prevention given bleeding risk.

PROBLEMS
P1 Therapeutic duplication: two sulfonylureas (glimepiride + gliclazide) from different prescribers -> hypoglycaemia.
P2 Metformin above renal limit for eGFR 30-44 (max 1000 mg/day).
P3 Hyperkalaemia on telmisartan + spironolactone; no current indication for spironolactone on file.

RECOMMENDATIONS (discussed by phone with Dr. Contractor on 12/10/26 at 3:40 pm; copy e-mailed to Dr. K.V.S. at kvsubramaniam.neph@navjeevanhosp.in)
- Stop gliclazide; glimepiride reduced to 1 mg 1-0-0, review SMBG chart.
- Metformin 500 mg 1-0-1.
- Stop spironolactone; repeat K+ and creatinine after 1 week.
- Continue dapagliflozin, telmisartan, atorvastatin.
- Withhold herbal product; Mr. Engineer to bring the pack.
Next review: 19th October 2026.

Reviewed by : Ms. Deepa Thomas, Pharm.D., Clinical Pharmacist (MSPC Reg. No. 74512)

dialogue:
[pharmacist] morning , tess . i'm here for the monthly review on 214-b , mrs . dufresne-okafor .
[nurse] oh , lise ? she's doing better . she had that fall on october 11th , out in the courtyard .
[pharmacist] what happened exactly ?
[nurse] she tripped over the garden hose while she was watering the tomato planters . no head strike , she landed on the right knee . dr . walker saw her that afternoon .
[pharmacist] she's on apixaban 2.5 , so did anyone look for a bleed ?
[nurse] x-ray was negative . big bruise on the knee . the ultrasound showed a baker's cyst behind it , nothing acute .
[pharmacist] was she using her walker ?
[nurse] no , she'd parked the walker by the bench . she's 91 , she does what she wants .
[pharmacist] fair enough . i still see zolpidem 5 mg at bedtime .
[nurse] she asks for it every night . her daughter colette says she's been on it since she lived in eau claire .
[pharmacist] i'll recommend a taper . any morning grogginess ?
[nurse] a bit foggy before breakfast . her morse fall scale came back at 65 .
[pharmacist] that's high risk . and oxybutynin 5 mg twice a day is still on the mar ?
[nurse] yes .
[pharmacist] strongly anticholinergic at her age . i'll suggest mirabegron and fax the review to dr . walker today .
[nurse] sounds good . colette's number is on the face sheet .

CONSULTANT PHARMACIST MEDICATION REGIMEN REVIEW (MRR) - POST-FALL
Facility: Maple Crest Health & Rehabilitation, 815 Linden Terrace, Chippewa Falls, WI 54729   Room 214-B

MRN MC-55821   Medicare MBI 4TR7-KD2-HX58   Allergy: sulfa (rash)
Attending: Lionel Walker, MD   NPI 1659304872   Fax (715) 555-0162
POA: Colette Brandt (daughter) 715-555-0139
Reviewer: Priya Natarajan, PharmD, BCGP, Northwoods Consultant Pharmacy, pnatarajan@northwoodsrx.com
Review date: 15 Oct 2026

HISTORY
91-year-old woman, retired French teacher (St. Bernadette Academy), resident since 2022. PMH: atrial fibrillation (CHA2DS2-VASc 5), overactive bladder, insomnia, OA. On Oct 11, 2026 she tripped over the garden hose while watering tomato planters in the courtyard and fell onto the right knee; no head strike, no LOC. Front-wheeled walker not in use. Seen same day by Dr. Walker.

FINDINGS
Right knee contusion with ecchymosis; X-ray negative. Ultrasound (accession US-26-0048817, 10/12/2026): Baker's cyst, no hematoma. BP 132/70, HR 74 irregular. Wt 54 kg, SCr 1.1, Hgb 12.1. Morse Fall Scale 65; MMSE 24/30. Night nurse Tess Baker, RN reports nightly zolpidem requests and AM grogginess.

CURRENT REGIMEN / ASSESSMENT
- Apixaban 2.5 mg BID: reduced dose appropriate (age >= 80, weight <= 60 kg). Continue; watch knee for bleeding.
- Metoprolol tartrate 25 mg BID: continue; hold for HR < 55 or SBP < 100.
- Zolpidem 5 mg QHS: listed in 2023 AGS Beers Criteria; falls, next-day sedation.
- Oxybutynin IR 5 mg BID: strongly anticholinergic (Beers list).
- Acetaminophen 650 mg q6h PRN, max 3 g/day.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Zolpidem 2.5 mg QHS x 14 days, then stop.
2. Change oxybutynin to mirabegron 25 mg daily; recheck BP in 2 weeks.
3. Keep walker within reach; PT gait re-evaluation.
4. Re-review in 30 days or after any fall.
